name: Excalidraw MCP (official MCP App + community mcp_excalidraw)
tagline: Agents draw, inspect and edit Excalidraw diagrams over MCP

license.notes: Official excalidraw-mcp README says MIT but the repo has no LICENSE file (GitHub reports no license). Community mcp_excalidraw is MIT with a LICENSE file. Excalidraw itself is MIT.

backing: Official: Excalidraw (company behind excalidraw.com; repo originated as antonpk1/excalidraw-mcp-app). Community: individual (yctimlin) with 25 contributors.

adoption.downloads: Community mcp-excalidraw-server: 5,145/week npm (2026-10-01..07). @excalidraw/excalidraw: 675,606/week npm. Official MCP is mainly used via the hosted remote endpoint (no download count).
adoption.summary: Official MCP App: 5.5k stars, 518 forks, works in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Goose. Community server: 2.5k stars, actively released (v2.1.x, Oct 2026).

maintainability.recent_activity: Official: none since 2026-03-24. Community: 35 commits since 2026-07-11, pushed 2026-10-09
maintainability.bus_factor: low for both: official is a small widget side project; community is one main maintainer
maintainability.summary: The official MCP App was a burst in February 2026; the community server is the actively maintained, more capable one.

architecture.summary: Official: an MCP Apps server with two tools, read_me (format cheat-sheet) and create_view (a JSON array of Excalidraw elements rendered into a ui:// iframe with draw-on animation and camera moves). It is a declarative re-send model: each create_view returns a checkpointId; later calls start with {type:'restoreCheckpoint', id} and add elements or {type:'delete', ids} pseudo-elements, and user edits in fullscreen are saved back to the checkpoint. Community: a local canvas server (Excalidraw web UI + REST + WebSocket sync) fronted by an MCP stdio server with 26 tools, a CLI with JSON in/out, and an agent skill; screenshots render headlessly since v2.1.
key_points: Scene is a JSON array of elements with ids; .excalidraw files are portable artifacts
Official tools: read_me, create_view; checkpoints + delete pseudo-elements; 'animation mode' (delete and replace in place with camera nudges)

Community tools: create_element, get_element, update_element, delete_element, query_elements, batch_create_elements, duplicate_elements, align/distribute/group/ungroup/lock/unlock, describe_scene, get_canvas_screenshot, export_scene, import_scene, export_to_image, export_to_excalidraw_url, create_from_mermaid, clear_canvas, snapshot_scene, restore_snapshot, set_viewport, read_diagram_guide, get_resource
Community readback: describe (structured text: ids, positions, labels, connections) and screenshot (PNG/SVG)
Community state: in-memory by default, EXCALIDRAW_DATA_DIR for restart recovery; named snapshots

agent_usability.how: MCP (official: remote https://mcp.excalidraw.com or local stdio, MCP Apps UI; community: stdio MCP 26 tools, CLI `npx -y mcp-excalidraw-server <cmd>`, REST API).
agent_usability.integration_effort: One connector URL (official) or one `claude mcp add` / npx command (community).
agent_usability.readback: Official: none for the model beyond its own checkpoints. Community: describe_scene (structured) and get_canvas_screenshot (image).
agent_usability.granular_edits: Official: coarse (restore checkpoint, delete by id, append). Community: per-element update by id, query by type/bbox/filter.
agent_usability.history: Official: checkpoints per create_view. Community: named snapshots save/list/restore. Excalidraw's own undo/redo is human-facing.
agent_usability.summary: The community server is a near-complete 'agent-editable live canvas' with structured and visual readback; the official one is a polished one-shot widget.

score_notes.ui_as_data: the diagram is entirely a JSON element list (it is a diagram, not an app UI)
score_notes.agent_drivable: community server: create/change/operate a live canvas via MCP, CLI or REST
score_notes.granular_edits: community update_element by id; official only coarse checkpoint/delete
score_notes.time_travel: checkpoints/named snapshots the agent can restore; no history log or seek
score_notes.live_data_rate: WebSocket sync of agent-paced edits; no data streams
score_notes.maturity: official widely reachable but dormant since March; community actively used (5k npm/week)
score_notes.openness: MIT, controlled by a company (official) or one maintainer (community)

steelman: Excalidraw over MCP is the cleanest proof that 'the picture is a JSON value' makes agents good at visual work. The official MCP App needed only two tools and a cheat-sheet to get agents in Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code drawing animated, hand-drawn diagrams inline, and its checkpoint plus delete-pseudo-element trick is a token-cheap patch protocol that even supports in-place animation. The community server goes all the way: 26 tools for per-element CRUD, layout, structured scene description and headless screenshots, so an agent draws, looks, fixes truncated labels and looks again; diagrams export as .excalidraw files into the repo. It is MIT, trivial to install, and actively used.
weaknesses: Diagrams, not application UIs: no input widgets, data binding or keyboard-driven apps
Official server: model cannot see the canvas or user edits except via checkpoints; dormant since March 2026; no LICENSE file despite MIT claim
Community server: in-memory by default; Mermaid conversion still needs a browser tab
No real history log or replay, only snapshots

relation_to_scene.overlap: Whole surface as a JSON value, id-addressed element edits, structured plus rendered readback, snapshots, agent-driven animation and explanation.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Little for scene's core, but the community server's draw-look-fix loop and the official checkpoint/delete patch format are proven agent ergonomics scene should mirror rather than reinvent.
borrow: A read_me / guide tool that returns the format cheat-sheet before first use
Checkpoint ids returned from every push so the agent can say 'start from checkpoint X, delete ids a,b, add these' instead of resending
describe_scene: a compact text description (ids, positions, labels, connections) distinct from the raw screen
query_elements by type/bbox/filter for addressing scene nodes
Named snapshots save/list/restore as a stopgap before full time travel
relation_to_scene.gap_left: No terminal rendering, no app interactivity (keys, focus, lists), no live data sources, no hot-swap; scene is a running terminal application, not a diagram.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Different medium, but its agent protocol details (cheat-sheet tool, checkpoint-relative patches, describe vs screenshot) are battle-tested patterns scene can copy.
